pages.title: Mango Bush
pages.text: $(item)A super genetically-modified variety$(0) — once a towering fruit tree, now reduced to a waist-high shrub. Plant a $(item)mango$(0) on dirt and it will take root, growing through four stages before bearing ripe fruit. $(br)Right-click to harvest mangoes once mature; the bush then returns to its young stage to grow again. $(br)Beware passing through: the dense foliage snags travelers and slows them to a crawl.

pages.title: Mutation Notes
pages.text: Mango trees once rose into the clouds, their fruit hanging far out of reach. Then the wave of genetic modification swept the fields, and everything changed: trunks shortened into stems, canopies shrank into bushes, and fruit now dangles at waist height. $(br)Some sneer that this is degeneration, but the bushes ripen faster and yield more — anyone can simply reach out and pick. Who still cares whether it is truly a tree?
